heading: Clipboard, share, notifications and geolocation
body:
Four browser APIs need the user's consent, so a project must grant them first. List them in `tac.browserApis` in `client/manifest.json`. A call to an API that is not granted fails at once with a message that names the grant. Tachyon adds nothing to a page that grants nothing.

| API | Calls (JavaScript names) | Needs a click or key handler | The answer arrives as |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Clipboard` (grant `clipboard`) | `writeText(text)`, `readText()` | Yes | `ClipboardTextRead { text }` after `readText` |
| `Share` (grant `share`) | `open(title, text, url)` | Yes | `ShareFinished {}` |
| `Notifications` (grant `notifications`) | `permission()`, `requestPermission()`, `show(title, body)` | `requestPermission` only | `NotificationPermissionChanged { permission }` |
| `Geolocation` (grant `geolocation`) | `currentPosition()` | No | `PositionFound { latitude, longitude, accuracy, timestamp }` |

JavaScript and TypeScript get them with `@Needs clipboard`, `@Needs share`, `@Needs notifications` and `@Needs geolocation`. Rust fields such as `clipboard: Clipboard` are filled by `Default`, Go uses `// @Needs` fields, C# `new()` fields, F# `let clipboard = Clipboard()` bindings, Dart `@Needs()` fields, Swift `private let clipboard = Clipboard()` fields, Java `private final Clipboard clipboard = new Clipboard();` fields, C++ `[[Needs]] Clipboard& clipboard;` fields, and Ruby `Clipboard.new`. Lua calls the global tables with `:`, such as `Clipboard:write_text(text)`, and needs no field. The names follow each language: `write_text` in Rust, Ruby and Lua, `WriteText` in Go, C# and F#, `writeText` in Dart, Java, Kotlin, Swift and C++. A Java call that the page refuses at once throws an `IllegalStateException`, a C# or F# call an `InvalidOperationException`, and a C++ call a `std::runtime_error`. A Lua call raises a Lua error; catch it with `pcall`. Swift names its arguments: `open(title:text:url:)` and `show(title:body:)`, and every call is used with `try`.

The browser answers these calls later, so the call itself only starts the work. The answer is a built-in event model, and Tachyon sends it to the service that made the call, not to every listener. Write an `@OnEvent` listener for the model. When the browser refuses or fails after the call started (the user says no, or no position is found), the service gets `BrowserCallFailed { api, call, message }` instead. `permission()` and `show(title, body)` answer at once; `show` fails until the user has allowed notifications.

The browser allows the clipboard, sharing and the notification question only right after the user clicks or presses a key. Call them from a method that the view runs on a click. Every call to the page is synchronous, so a Rust, Go, C#, F#, Dart, Ruby, Lua, Swift or C++ method that a click runs still counts as the click. A call without a user action fails at once with "The clipboard browser API needs a user action. Call it from a click or key handler." A call made after an `await` in Dart may no longer be tied to its service; its answer then goes to every listener of the model. Python has no tab: a Python service has no browser APIs yet, and a Python service that uses one stops the build with `TY1605`.
